page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Microarchitecture capabilities include a 480 MB L3 cache as well as hardware instruction extensions for AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8).

Storage provisions include a 945 GB local NVMe SSD, and the platform supports Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators. In standardized testing, the system demonstrates strong single-threaded throughput in data handling tasks, reaching 32.42 GB/sec in single-core gzip compression and 13.98 GB/sec in single-core bzip3 decompression, both placing within the upper quartile of benchmarked instances.

Broader multi-core compute and memory metrics register within median ranges, including a PassMark CPU score of 26,945.67, static web serving throughput of 30.27 GB/sec, and 27.33 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. Small-model LLM text generation reaches 267.04 tokens per second. Given the lower memory-to-core density coupled with high-speed local NVMe disk space, this server type offers cost-effective execution for compute-centric workloads, data compression tasks, web servers, and build environments that do not require high per-vCPU RAM allocations.
description: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz across 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores. Configured with 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and a 480 MB L3 cache, the system features hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Local storage includes a 945 GB NVMe SSD, while no GPUs are attached. In benchmark evaluations, the instance registers upper-quartile performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.42 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.98 GB/sec, alongside median-tier marks in general multi-core stress testing and Redis key-value operations. The low-memory, local-disk configuration delivers high resource efficiency for CPU-heavy tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools, making it well matched for data compression pipelines, static web serving, build automation, and local scratch disk caching workloads.
